title: Start with a question and a safe search
objectives: Identify the manual YL2 Search context and the external site's privacy boundary.
Construct an event-type filter and narrow it to an exact symbolic user.
Distinguish a compiled query, a returned event, and a justified conclusion.
story: Signal Desk assigns your first practice task: examine login telemetry for an authorized identity. This is a learning exercise, not an allegation about a real user. Select the identity privately in SecOps; the training site calls it [USER].

teaching.heading: A filter is a question about events
teaching.text: A SIEM correlation filter decides which normalized events are relevant. A Search filter does the same initial selection without deploying a rule. Start by asking for USER_LOGIN events. metadata.event_type names the normalized event category; it is not a vendor's raw event ID. The string enum is quoted and uses its documented uppercase value.

teaching.heading: Choose the correct editor and range
teaching.text: In workplace SecOps, use manual Search in the YL2 dialect and choose an authorized short time range using the UI. Do not use natural-language/Gemini generation as part of this AI-free course. Search range is a separate UI control, not a value the training site collects. Your tenant may use older UI wording.

teaching.heading: Symbols are not variables
teaching.text: The training symbol [USER] serializes as the synthetic string "__USER__". Only inside SecOps do you replace it with an approved value. A YARA-L variable such as $user is a different concept taught later. Never paste the substituted query or its results back here.

teaching.heading: Empty results are evidence with limits
teaching.text: Compiler success only establishes that the platform accepts the query. An empty result might reflect time range, permissions, normalization, ingestion delay, or no matching activity. It is not proof that a person is safe or malicious. Inspect available event details and field mapping privately.

challenges.title: Find the event category
challenges.prompt: Construct a Search query selecting USER_LOGIN events. Return event rows, with no aggregate, condition, order, limit, or rule wrapper.
hints: Choose the normalized event category field, not a raw vendor event code.
Use metadata.event_type, equality, and the quoted USER_LOGIN enum.

methodQuestions.prompt: Where should this query be run?

options.label: Manual SecOps Search with YL2 selected
The detection Rules editor as a new deployed rule
A query box on this external training site

methodQuestions.rationale: This lesson is interactive Search. The training site checks symbolic structure and never executes SIEM queries.

methodQuestions.prompt: The query runs and returns no events. What is the best next step?

options.label: Declare there were no logins anywhere
Check the range, access, data availability, and normalization inside SecOps
Upload a raw log here so the site can repair it

methodQuestions.rationale: Zero results have several possible causes. Troubleshooting stays inside authorized workplace tools.

executeSteps: Open the already-approved SecOps environment manually; do not enter its URL here.
Select YL2 and an authorized short time range.
Run the category query and inspect any available normalized event in SecOps.
If no events return, check range, permissions and available telemetry; widen only within policy.
challenges.debrief: State privately what this filter establishes and one thing it cannot establish. On the site, attest only that it ran and the result or limitation was reviewed.

challenges.title: Narrow to an exact actor identity
challenges.prompt: Select USER_LOGIN events whose principal.user.userid exactly equals [USER]. Exact case-sensitive matching is required. Return event rows without further sections.
hints: Add an identity constraint to the category filter; both must hold.
The training actor identity field is principal.user.userid. Use [USER] and AND.

methodQuestions.prompt: What should you verify before substituting a real value?

options.label: That the user field is populated and represents the intended role in this log source
That every source places usernames in principal
That a display name always equals userid

methodQuestions.rationale: The dictionary defines the field, but the parser/source determines which role and identifier are populated.

methodQuestions.prompt: Where do you replace __USER__ and keep observations?

options.label: Only in workplace SecOps and approved workplace notes

methodQuestions.rationale: Real values and observations never enter this external training app.

executeSteps: Choose an authorized identity inside SecOps; do not record the mapping on this site.
Inspect the actual source's UDM mapping before applying principal.user.userid.
Replace __USER__ only in SecOps and run the narrowed query.
If that source maps the relevant user to target instead, adapt privately and record the mapping in workplace notes; the scored symbolic task still teaches the specified principal role.
challenges.debrief: Compare the broad and narrowed searches privately. Do not return row counts or usernames. Explain why a narrower search better answers this particular question.
